steps.title: Biological
steps.body: Fino ages under flor, giving pale, bone-dry wines with almond, bread and salt, at about 15%. Manzanilla is Fino aged in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, where cooler, humid sea air keeps flor thick, adding a saline, chamomile freshness. Both are best fresh, soon after bottling.

steps.title: Oxidative and in between
steps.body: Oloroso, fortified to 17%, ages with oxygen, turning amber-brown with walnut, toffee and spice, yet dry. Amontillado starts as Fino, then loses its flor and ages oxidatively, combining both styles. Palo Cortado is rare: it loses flor early, giving Amontillado's aroma with Oloroso's body. Cream Sherry is sweetened, often with Pedro Ximénez.

steps.prompt: Match each Sherry to its ageing.
steps.explanation: The path of ageing defines the style.

steps.body: An opened bottle of Fino or Manzanilla behaves like a white wine: keep it in the fridge and finish it within a week.

steps.prompt: Which Sherry styles are naturally dry?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Fino and Manzanilla age under flor, pale and dry
Oloroso ages oxidatively, dark yet dry
Amontillado and Palo Cortado combine both paths
